chunks: In the narration of Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from some of his men, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
I asked him about the evidence when it is established over a right: is it permissible for the judge to rule by the statement of the evidence?
So he said: Five things are such that the people must act in them according to the outward ruling: the wilayahs, marriages, slaughtered animals, testimonies, and lineages.
So when a man's outward state is outwardly trustworthy, his testimony is permissible, and his inward state is not asked about.

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةِ: legal proof or evidentiary testimony used to establish a right
key_terms.الْحَقِّ: a rightful claim or due entitlement
key_terms.الْقَاضِي: the judge who issues a ruling
key_terms.الْوِلَايَاتُ: positions or matters of authority and recognized jurisdiction
key_terms.بَاطِنِهِ: a person's inward reality or hidden inner state
key_terms.بِظَاهِرِ الْحُكْمِ: according to the apparent legal ruling based on outward evidence

ai.seo_question: When can a judge rule by outward evidence and accept a witness without investigating his inner state?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle that certain matters are judged according to outward appearances and established evidence rather than hidden inner realities. It specifically includes authority-related matters, marriage, slaughtered animals, testimony, and lineage, and affirms that a person whose outward condition is trustworthy may have his testimony accepted without investigation into his inner state.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3244 - In the narration of Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (as):
I asked him about evidence when it is presented to establish a right-whether it is permissible for the judge to rule based on the testimony of the witnesses.
Imam (as) said: "There are five matters in which people must act according to apparent judgment: leadership positions, marriages, slaughtered animals, testimonies, and lineage.
So, if a man's outward appearance is trustworthy, his testimony is accepted, and his inner state is not investigated."
